about: Learn A10, Which emissions question are you asking? The Plains Grid's fleet (also read by A12 and M6), the day, the two loads, the long-run and procurement options, the card sort and the numbers to remember. The Plains Grid is fictional and its plant sizes are illustrative; the plants' heat rates, fuel prices and CO2 coefficients are EIA's, with their tables and dates in sources.

plains.name: Plains Grid
plains.note: Illustrative: a fictional regional grid with a 4,000 MW peak (as in lesson 3), much wind, some solar and gas plants. Not a model of any real grid.

heat.label: EIA, Electric Power Annual, Table 8.2: average tested heat rates by prime mover, 2025 (natural gas combined cycle 7,535 Btu per kWh; gas turbine 10,975), reported at full load
heat.asOf: 2025 data, release of 21 October 2026; read 5 November 2026

fuel.label: EIA, Electric Power Annual, Table 7.4: average cost of natural gas to the electric power industry, 2025 ($3.85 per MMBtu)

co2.label: EIA, Carbon Dioxide Emissions Coefficients: natural gas 52.91 kg CO₂ per MMBtu

vom.label: EIA, Assumptions to the Annual Energy Outlook 2026, Electricity Market Module, Table 3: variable O&M of a combined-cycle plant ($3.49 per MWh) and of a combustion turbine ($4.17), 2025 dollars

shapes.label: EIA, Hourly Electric Grid Monitor (Form EIA-930), Southwest Power Pool, 2025: hourly demand, wind and solar shapes

cf.label: EIA, Electric Power Monthly, Table 6.07.B: capacity factors in 2025, wind 33.8%, solar PV 24.0%, and the monthly values

ez.label: Electrolyzer
ez.how: runs at 300 MW in the 12 hours with the lowest average CO₂ factor, read from the grid without it (ties: the earlier hour)

newCC.source: EIA, AEO2026 Electricity Market Module, Table 3: a new combined-cycle plant (single shaft), heat rate 6,226 Btu per kWh, variable O&M $3.49 per MWh

procure.label: No purchase: the grid's average
procure.note: Location-based: each MWh at its hour's average factor.

procure.label: Certificates from an existing wind farm, matched over the year
procure.note: Assume the wind farm ran anyway: the purchase changes nothing on the grid.

procure.label: A new wind farm on another grid in the same certificate market, matched over the year
procure.note: Assume it is built for this buyer but its output enters another grid, not this one.

procure.label: A new wind farm on this grid, matched over the year
procure.note: Assume the purchase gets it built (additional) and no line limits (deliverable): its output enters this grid.

procure.label: The same new wind farm, matched hour by hour
procure.note: Hours its output falls short are counted at the grid average, a teaching proxy; a residual mix is left out.

claimRules.label: Illustrative reporting rules, after the GHG Protocol's Scope 2 Guidance (2015), market-based method
claimRules.assume: Each certificate is assumed to be this buyer's alone, retired for it, and from the same market as its use (Table 7.1, criteria 2, 3 and 5).
claimRules.proxy: Shortfall hours use the grid average as a teaching proxy; the guidance asks for a residual mix (the factor of unclaimed power) where one exists.
claimRules.status: The GHG Protocol consulted on a revision from 20 October 2025 to 31 January 2026; hourly matching and deliverability are proposals, not adopted rules (feedback summary, 29 July 2026).

sources.label: GHG Protocol, Scope 2 Guidance (2015), Table 7.1: Scope 2 Quality Criteria, page 60
GHG Protocol, Scope 2 Public Consultation Feedback Summary: Executive Summary

cards.text: The electrolyzer's share of the region's CO₂ in 2025.
cards.why: A share of a total that already happened: average factors, and the shares add up.

cards.text: Moving batch jobs to hours with a lower grid average shrinks the data center's footprint.
cards.why: Counted at average factors, so it is an attributed footprint, as in CF6, not a measured change at the plants.

cards.text: If the data center switches on tomorrow, how much more will the gas plants burn?
cards.why: The fleet is fixed and only output changes: marginal factors from a dispatch model.

cards.text: A dispatch model says each extra MWh at 03:00 comes from the combined-cycle plants.
cards.why: A marginal plant read from one model; another model's rules can name another plant.

cards.text: Over ten years, does the new load lead to more wind farms or more gas plants?
cards.why: What gets built in response: a planning model or a long-run marginal factor.

cards.text: A planning model adds the load and compares the build-out with and without it.
cards.why: Consequential through investment: the difference of two plans.

cards.text: We may report zero Scope 2 emissions because we bought certificates.
cards.why: A reporting rule for purchases: it sets what may be claimed, not what the plants do.

cards.text: Our contract matches every hour of use with a new solar farm on the same grid.
cards.why: Hourly matching with new supply on the same grid: a stricter claim, still a rule about the buyer's portfolio.

facts.what: CO₂ from burning natural gas, per million Btu of heat; a gas plant's CO₂ per MWh is this times its heat rate.
facts.label: EIA, Carbon Dioxide Emissions Coefficients
